transcript.answer:
Summary (short)
- Root cause: The ledger-api processes on one node hit the process file-descriptor limit (EMFILE / "Too many open files"), causing accept() to fail and the readiness probe to fail → those pods became NotReady.
- Scope: 3 of 6 replica pods (exact names below) on node rcabench-worker2 are affected; the 3 pods on rcabench-worker are healthy.

What I observed (evidence)
- Affected pods (all from the new rollout, APP_VERSION=1.4.2):
  - ledger-api-866db84748-2zjp4  — node: rcabench-worker2 — Ready: False
  - ledger-api-866db84748-cz4wp  — node: rcabench-worker2 — Ready: False
  - ledger-api-866db84748-vv6jk  — node: rcabench-worker2 — Ready: False
- Healthy pods (same deployment, different node):
  - ledger-api-866db84748-md6xh  — node: rcabench-worker — Ready: True
  - ledger-api-866db84748-r5mbh  — node: rcabench-worker — Ready: True
  - ledger-api-866db84748-xzjxb  — node: rcabench-worker — Ready: True
- Timeline:
  - Deployment rollout created ~2026-10-07T09:43:20Z; pods started ~2026-10-07T09:44:11–13Z.
  - Errors begin ~2026-10-07T09:45:33Z (≈1 minute after start) and repeat constantly.
- Application logs from affected pods (representative lines):
  - "2026-10-07T09:45:33Z ERROR ledger-api accept failed: [Errno 24] Too many open files"
  - This "[Errno 24] Too many open files" repeats every 10s–20s afterward.
- Pod events show readiness probe failures:
  - Initial: "Readiness probe failed: ... connect: connection refused"
  - Later: "Readiness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 503"
  - Readiness probe is configured as an HTTP GET to /healthz on port 8080 (timeout 1s).
- Node list: All nodes are Ready, but only rcabench-worker2 has the three failing pods.

Why this is the root cause
- Errno 24 is the operating-system error returned when a process has exhausted its allowed number of open file descriptors. The application is failing on accept() (socket accept) which directly prevents it from servicing the readiness probe and client connections.
- The failure is localized to pods on a single node (rcabench-worker2), which strongly implies a node-scoped limit or contention (node-level ulimits, container runtime limits, or other high FD usage on that node), not a global cluster networking failure.
- The timing (errors begin shortly after the new rollout) makes it possible that the new version increased concurrency / opened more sockets or exposed an existing FD leak, but the immediate mechanism making pods NotReady is the EMFILE condition on the process.

Suggested immediate remediation (what to do now)
1. Restore service quickly (choose one):
   - Drain and restart the affected node:
     - kubectl cordon rcabench-worker2
     - kubectl drain rcabench-worker2 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
     - Reboot or restart container runtime/kubelet on rcabench-worker2 (or power-cycle the host).
     - Uncordon when done: kubectl uncordon rcabench-worker2
   - Or restart the container runtime on that node (containerd) — this releases FDs for running containers and will cause pods to restart on healthy nodes.
   - If you prefer an application rollback while you investigate, roll back the deployment:
     - kubectl rollout undo deployment/ledger-api -n ledger
2. After restarting/recovering, re-check readiness and logs to confirm the error no longer appears.

Commands I recommend to run on rcabench-worker2 to confirm & diagnose
(you need node access / ssh or a debug privileged pod)
- Find the ledger-api process PID inside the container / node and count its FDs:
  - lsof -p <pid> | wc -l
  - ls -l /proc/<pid>/fd | wc -l
- Check process limits:
  - cat /proc/<pid>/limits   (look at "Max open files")
  - su -s /bin/sh -c 'ulimit -n' root  (or run on node shell)
- Check system/service limits for kubelet and containerd:
  - systemctl show -p LimitNOFILE kubelet
  - systemctl show -p LimitNOFILE containerd
- Check kernel/global max FDs:
  - sysctl fs.file-max
- Check for other heavy FD users on the node:
  - lsof | awk '{print $1}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head

Root-cause hypotheses to investigate (ranked)
1. Node-level ulimit too low on rcabench-worker2 or container runtime/kubelet systemd services set a small LimitNOFILE → containers inherit too-small FD limits → app hits limit. (Most likely given node-locality and EMFILE.)
2. Application-level file-descriptor leak or increased concurrency in 1.4.2 that drives FD usage above normal limits — would explain why the problem appeared after the rollout. (Possible; investigate code changes in 1.4.2 and FD counts.)
3. Some other process on rcabench-worker2 (outside these containers) is exhausting global resources, leaving fewer FDs available to container processes. (Less likely but check.)

Permanent fixes / recommendations
- Short-term: increase per-process file-descriptor limits on the node:
  - Set LimitNOFILE=65536 (or higher) for kubelet and containerd in systemd unit files and restart those services; or set system-wide ulimit via /etc/security/limits.conf and ensure it's applied to container runtime and kubelet.
  - Example: add/modify /etc/systemd/system/kubelet.service.d/10-limit.conf:
    - [Service]
      LimitNOFILE=65536
    - Then systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl restart kubelet
  - Do the same for containerd if needed.
- Medium-term:
  - Investigate the app (1.4.2) for FD leaks: enable FD metrics, run lsof/perf whilst under load, and review code paths that open files/sockets (batching, connection pooling).
  - Add instrumentation/alerts for process FD usage so you catch EMFILE before readiness breaks.
  - Consider liveness probe behavior: keep liveness probes that restart the pod if it becomes unhealthy and cannot recover.
- Long-term:
  - Add node-level capacity checks and run the deployment with a smaller per-node pod skew so a single-node problem cannot affect half the replicas (spread across more nodes).
  - If the new version increased concurrency, tune the app to limit simultaneous connections or increase resource allowances.

If you want I can:
- Check the deployment revision history and provide the exact previous image/tag to roll back to.
- Run commands to inspect FD and system limits from a debug privileged pod if you permit me to run a debug pod on rcabench-worker2.
- Draft the exact systemd snippets/commands you should apply to kubelet/containerd on rcabench-worker2.

Would you like me to (A) produce the exact rollback commands and previous revision, (B) attempt live node checks (I’ll need permission to run a debug pod on that node), or (C) draft systemd edits to raise LimitNOFILE for kubelet/containerd?
